title: Search-Anchored Hybrid Rollouts for Text-Based World Models

contributions.purpose: Diagnose the root cause of rollout drift in LLM-based world models for web agents.
contributions.mechanism: Systematic error analysis of world-model rollouts on WebShop, localizing where simulated trajectories first diverge from real environment behavior.
contributions.evaluation: 100% of first divergences occur at search-result observations, with search results exhibiting a 99.8% per-step divergence rate.
contributions.domain: LLM world models for web agents
contributions.source_quote: We identify search-result simulation as the primary failure mode in LLM-based world models for web agents, with 100% of first divergences occurring at search observations.

contributions.purpose: Mitigate rollout drift without improving the world model itself.
contributions.mechanism: Search-anchored hybrid rollouts intercept search actions and substitute the world model's predicted search results with actual cached WebShop search-engine results, keeping all other observations simulated.
contributions.evaluation: Improves Consistency Ratio on WebShop from 0.594 to 0.824 (+38.7% relative), outperforming agent-side baselines such as Best-of-N sampling and ReAct prompting.
contributions.domain: LLM world models for web agents
contributions.source_quote: We propose search-anchored hybrid rollouts, a minimal intervention that grounds only search observations while retaining efficient simulation for other action types.

contributions.purpose: Quantify the benefit of grounding all searches versus only the first, showing compounding search errors drive drift.
contributions.mechanism: Ablation comparing anchoring only the first search (CR = 0.598, negligible benefit) against anchoring all searches, with analysis over multi-search episodes.
contributions.evaluation: +38.7% Consistency Ratio improvement on WebShop, with benefits scaling for multi-search episodes that comprise approximately 90% of tasks.
contributions.domain: LLM world models for web agents
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate +38.7% improvement in Consistency Ratio on WebShop, with benefits scaling for multi-search episodes that comprise approximately 90% of tasks.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work differs by identifying search-result simulation as the specific failure mode and proposing targeted grounding rather than general retrieval augmentation.

Our search-anchored hybrid rollouts apply this principle to text-based world models: rather than improving the world model's ability to simulate all observations, we ground only the high-entropy search observations that drive rollout drift, while retaining efficient simulation for structured state updates.
